applicability.scope: Source-grounded audit of native image-generation weight/runtime residency, optional segment prefetch and bounded non-ZIP safetensors catalog/read/staging ownership; confirm the actual source, GGML, backend, model and executing path independently.
applicability.prerequisites: Access to the pinned source/storage boundaries and evidence of the actual image runner/backend dispatch; native capacity or prefetch checks require matching GGML, model and backend resources.
applicability.input_contract: Runtime/GGML revisions and selection, compiled/loaded backends and devices, model/components and numerical image settings, effective memory/prefetch/placement settings and actual dispatch; retain available phase allocations, cache/workspace, transfer events and completed-image counts.
applicability.produced_artifact: A phase-by-runner/backend/device ownership table for stored and resident weights, retained runtime, pending allocations, pin/prefetch ownership and release/eviction, with one discriminating check and its actual status.
applicability.failure_modes: Treating max_vram as proof of segmentation, unpin as physical freeing, or configured prefetch as completed useful overlap can misidentify the capacity cause; missing observations cannot be read as zero.
applicability.refusal_point: Stop when the cause is resolved or matching GGML/model/backend resources are unavailable; invoking this audit does not authorize dependency installation, model downloads, policy changes or device provisioning.

limitations: Source-derived candidate; native inference, allocator behavior, image quality and performance were not run.

Eighteen bounded readset paths plus one separately identity-checked README match the pinned Git commit/tree blob IDs and sizes (19 blobs total); header coverage is limited to selected owner/state declarations, and this does not authenticate every archive member or submodule contents.

The loader/storage extension separately authenticates twelve bounded C++ source blobs and the retained MIT text; its line-scoped readset does not replace the historical archive receipt. Catalog stamps are not content hashes; read/mapping/backend calls do not establish storage throughput or device completion.
GGML and other submodules are not expanded; matching private GGML headers are required even for a system library.
CPU bypasses the inspected accelerator capacity gate and segmentation eligibility, so CPU checks cannot qualify accelerator memory budgets or prefetch.
Video/audio pipelines, detailed model kernels, approximate denoising caches and full multi-device execution remain outside this readset.
Loader rules select ordinary non-ZIP safetensors; full GGUF/Torch/ZIP parsers, special quantization/conversion correctness and native failure injection remain unqualified.
recommendations: Separate parameter storage, compute-resident weights, retained workspace/output caches and pending allocations for each runner and phase.
Verify the actual monolithic, segmented or multi-device path before interpreting a memory budget or prefetch setting.
For a policy comparison, hold model, inputs, numerical settings and device fixed; check completed images and quality before latency, and separate startup, first and warm requests.
